title: Schelling's segregation model: weak preferences, strong aggregate outcomes
body:
In Schelling's residential segregation model, even a mild same-group preference at the individual level produces strong spatial separation at the population level.
[Step] Simulation
  [Input] 50×50 lattice, tolerance threshold 30%, [Tool] NetLogo
[Step] Observation
  [Output] at tolerance 30%, large mono-type clusters form within ~100 steps
The model is the canonical illustration that micro-preferences and macro-outcomes can diverge. Real-world segregation is shaped by additional channels (discrimination, income, institutions), so using Schelling alone as empirical evidence overreaches what the model can support.
